The test image shows classic **interveinal chlorosis and necrosis** on soybean leaves - yellow areas between the veins progressing to brown necrotic patches, while the midvein and major lateral veins remain distinctly green. This is the hallmark foliar symptom of Sudden Death Syndrome.

Key distinguishing features:
- Large chlorotic/necrotic blotches confined between veins
- Veins remain green while interveinal tissue dies
- Multiple leaves in the upper canopy affected
- No purple/bronze discoloration (rules out Cercospora)
- Not vein-associated necrosis (rules out Soybean Vein Necrosis)
- Pattern is interveinal blotches, not general mottling (rules out viral diseases)
